title: Offline vs online evaluation
summary: Offline evaluation runs a fixed dataset with reference answers before release. Online evaluation scores sampled live traffic without references after release. You need both, joined by a loop that turns production failures into new test cases.
useIf: You must decide which checks gate a release and which keep watching after it.
avoidIf: You are tempted to use either one alone: offline alone misses drift, online alone lets users find regressions.

explain.md: **Offline** evaluation runs a candidate over dataset examples that carry reference outputs. It suits benchmarking, regression checks, unit tests and backtesting, and it is repeatable, so two versions can be compared on identical inputs. **Online** evaluation scores production runs and threads as they arrive. They have no reference outputs, so it checks quality patterns, safety and anomalies [[r29]].

Online scoring runs on logged traces asynchronously, so it adds no latency to the user request. Without ground truth it relies on reference-free judges [[r30]]. Foundry frames three lifecycle stages: base model selection, pre-production evaluation and post-production monitoring. The last covers operational metrics, continuous evaluation of sampled live traffic, scheduled evaluation on a test set to detect drift, scheduled red teaming and Azure Monitor alerts [[r1]].

explain.title: The loop between offline and online
explain.alt: An offline golden set gates a release, live traffic is scored online, and failing production traces flow back into the offline set.

explain.md: Foundry continuous evaluation is preview as checked on 2026-10-13. Its documented default is 100 runs per hour (`max_hourly_runs`), and runs are skipped once that cap is reached [[r7]]. Intelligent sampling dedupes, drops broken traces and picks diverse ones without extra model calls [[r40]].

whereToUse: Release gates in CI, where a fixed dataset makes versions comparable
Model or prompt upgrades, where you backtest on a set built from past traffic
Production dashboards that sample traces and score groundedness and safety
Drift detection on a schedule when the input mix changes
Triage queues that feed low-scoring traces back into the golden set

use: Offline when you can write or mine reference answers
Online when traffic is large and real inputs differ from your set
Both when a regression is costly and the user mix moves
avoid: Online-only when harm happens before anyone notices
Offline-only when the corpus or users change weekly
Scoring every live trace with a large judge when sampling would do
flips: Privacy rules forbid reading live content: keep online scoring to metadata and redacted text, or skip it
Traffic is tiny: online samples are too few, so lean on offline sets and human review
No traces exist yet (pre-launch): offline only, built from hand-written and synthetic cases

pitfalls.symptom: Online scores stop updating on busy days
pitfalls.cause: The continuous evaluation hourly cap was hit and runs were skipped
pitfalls.fix: Raise `max_hourly_runs`, lower the sampling rate on purpose, or alert on skipped runs

pitfalls.symptom: Offline score stays green while users complain
pitfalls.cause: The golden set no longer resembles real queries
pitfalls.fix: Feed failing and low-feedback traces back into the set and refresh on a schedule

pitfalls.symptom: A privacy review blocks online scoring
pitfalls.cause: Judges read real prompts and responses
pitfalls.fix: Redact before scoring, restrict access to results, set retention, and sample rather than score everything

scenarios.title: New assistant, nothing in production
scenarios.situation: A team is two weeks from the first release of a document Q&A assistant. There is no traffic, a corpus of a few thousand documents and one subject expert.
constraints: Reference answers can be written for a small set
unknowns: How harmful is a wrong answer?
Can the first users be a small pilot group?
scenarios.question: Which checks do you put in place before launch?

options.name: Offline set of hand-written and synthetic cases, plus a pilot with sampled online scoring after launch
options.why: It gates the release with references and prepares the online loop that will catch what the set misses.
options.tradeoff: The first set is guessed, so early scores overstate how real users will fare.

options.name: Online scoring only, starting at launch
options.why: There would be no regression gate, so the first users find the failures.
options.tradeoff: Online-only fits an internal tool with instant rollback and low harm.

options.name: A 2,000-case synthetic set judged by five judges
options.tradeoff: Large cost, and unreviewed synthetic rows can be easy or wrong.

flips.if: The pilot users are named staff who can report errors
flips.then: A lighter offline set is enough because feedback is quick.
Add red teaming and a human-reviewed safety slice before launch.

scenarios.takeaway: Before launch you only have offline. Plan the online loop before launch.

scenarios.title: Mature assistant, heavy traffic, sensitive content
scenarios.situation: An assistant handles millions of conversations a month over confidential documents. Quality has drifted twice after content updates. Security restricts who may read stored prompts.
unknowns: How quickly must drift be seen?
scenarios.question: How do you monitor quality without exposing content or overspending?

options.name: Sample and redact traces, score with reference-free judges, schedule an offline drift run
options.why: Sampling controls cost, redaction answers security, and the scheduled offline run catches drift with references.
options.tradeoff: Rare failures can fall between samples and redaction may blur some context.

options.name: Score every trace with the strongest judge
options.why: The cost is large and it reads all confidential content.
options.tradeoff: It is right only for a low-volume, high-stakes service with approved content access.

options.name: Rely on thumbs up and down alone
options.why: Cheap and needs no content reading.
options.tradeoff: Feedback is sparse and biased toward vocal users, so quality can drift unseen.

flips.if: Volume falls to a few hundred requests a day
flips.then: Review all or most traces by hand and drop sampling.

flips.if: Content may not be stored at all
flips.then: Score inside the request path on metadata and safety signals only.

scenarios.takeaway: At scale, sampling and redaction are the cost and privacy controls.

quiz.q: Why can online evaluation not use reference-based metrics?
options: Online runs are too slow for metrics
Live requests have no reference output to compare against
The judge cannot see the response
quiz.explain: Production runs carry no gold answer, so online scoring uses reference-free judges and safety checks. Online scoring is asynchronous, so speed is not the issue.

quiz.q: Online quality scores flatline during a traffic peak, yet nothing in the app changed. What do you check first?
options: Whether the golden set has been versioned
Whether the continuous evaluation hourly run cap was reached and runs were skipped
Whether the judge prompt has few-shot examples
quiz.explain: The documented default is 100 runs per hour and runs are skipped at the cap. The others do not explain a flatline tied to traffic.

quiz.q: Order the loop that keeps an evaluation set fresh.
items: Gate the release on the offline set
Add confirmed failures to the offline set
quiz.explain: The gate comes first, then live sampling and scoring, then human triage so only confirmed failures enter the set.

flashcards.front: What can offline evaluation use that online cannot?
flashcards.back: Reference outputs. Offline examples carry gold answers, so reference-based metrics and exact comparisons work. Online traces have none.

flashcards.front: How does Foundry label its three lifecycle stages?
flashcards.back: Base model selection, pre-production evaluation and post-production monitoring, which adds continuous evaluation, scheduled evaluation, scheduled red teaming and alerts.

flashcards.front: What is the cost control for online scoring?
flashcards.back: Sampling rate and filters. Each scored trace costs judge tokens, so sample, dedupe and cap runs per hour.
